content.thinking: This looks like silent data corruption from a bad deployment that removed the month total maintenance code, causing stored totals to be wrong rather than a visible outage—metrics stay flat and the error traces back to the oldest affected record. I'm weighing whether to cite the revision or the file path as the subject, leaning toward the revision.

hypotheses.subject: 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2
hypotheses.summary: Revision 26f1d7e deployed at 2026-10-17T23:08Z changed record_purchase so it no longer maintains the per-shopper month total. Totals written from then on disagree with the purchases behind them. The service keeps serving normally, so no request-level metric moved. The oldest affected purchase is at 23:10Z, two minutes after the deploy.

supporting_evidence.claim: Deploy 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2 modified src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py: removed the total_this_month_cents update from record_purchase ('The month is no longer carried')
Alert: 240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile; oldest affected purchase recorded at 2026-10-17T23:10:00Z. Error rate, latency and volume are flat across the window.
Rollout converged: all 3 replicas run 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2, so this is not a version split.

hypotheses.subject: 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2
hypotheses.summary: The deployed code change itself is the fault. It dropped the month-total update in record_purchase, so stored totals diverge from the purchase history.

supporting_evidence.claim: Revision 26f1d7e modified src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py, removing the total_this_month_cents maintenance, and the rollout has converged
